title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 81-84): Grothendieck axiomatizes 'polynomial categories' P. These have objects X, Y and sets P_n(X,Y) of 'polynomial maps of degree n', with P_1 the linear (additive) part. In a tensor setting P_n(X,Y)=Hom(Γ^n X, Y). Composition P_p×P_q→P_{pq} is g∘f = g·Γ^q(f)·α^X_{q,p}, where α_{q,p}: Γ^{pq}X→Γ^qΓ^pX. So degrees multiply under composition. In modern terms this is a category enriched over (N,×)-graded sets, a many-object analogue of a plethory, built from Roby-type polynomial laws.

This page does three things.
(1) Multi-variable polynomial maps. Let X = ⊕_{1≤i≤r} X_i (a biproduct, so also ∏X_i). The exponential 'diagonal' of divided powers, Γ^n(⊕X_i) → ⊕_{|ν|=n} ⊗_i Γ^{ν_i}(X_i), induces maps P_n(∏X_i, Y) → P_{ν_1,…,ν_r}(X_1,…,X_r;Y) := Hom(⊗Γ^{ν_i}X_i, Y). This is the decomposition of a degree-n polynomial map on a product into multihomogeneous components.
(2) Two definitions. He recalls what was used: the material of §1, that the tensor products of P_1 are strict (a special case of functors), and that the Γ^{ν} exist and satisfy the preliminary universal/associativity condition. He then defines a polynomial category P to be *strict* if it satisfies the preliminary conditions allowing ⊗ and Γ^n to be defined with all the envisaged properties. Separately, an additive category with ⊗, functors Γ^n and the structures above (α_{p,q}, diagonals, etc.) is called a '⊗-pd-category'. He asserts the two notions are essentially equivalent. This is a reconstruction statement: abstract polynomial-map data ⇔ a tensor category with divided-power functors representing them.
(3) k-linearity (continued on p.84). P is k-linear if a ring homomorphism k → End(id_{P_1}) is given such that the diagonal respects the gradings. Concretely, f ∈ P_{ν_1…ν_r} implies f∘(λ_1×…×λ_r) = λ_1^{ν_1}…λ_r^{ν_r} f, i.e. multihomogeneity of multidegree ν.

Purpose: inside a file on dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. The aim is presumably an abstract framework in which divided/symmetric powers of perfect complexes (Dold–Puppe style) and λ/γ-operations act functorially, as needed for multiplicative structures on K-theory and determinants. The next page gives modules over a ringed topos as the example and asks for PD structures Γ^p(Γ^q M) → Γ^{pq}M.
errors: The diagonal Γ^n(⊕X_i) lands in ⊕_{|ν|=n} ⊗Γ^{ν_i}(X_i), not in a single ⊗Γ^{ν_i}(X_i). So P_n(∏X_i,Y) maps to the product over all multidegrees ν with |ν|=n of P_ν, i.e. one component per ν. The page writes it for a fixed ν, which is acceptable only if read componentwise.

The claimed equivalence between 'strict polynomial category' and '⊗-pd-category' is only asserted, not proved. Representability of polynomial maps by Γ^n (à la Roby) needs the 'preliminary conditions'. These are said on p.82 to have been partly forgotten (e.g. the unit map 1→Γ^q(1)), so the axiom list is acknowledged to be incomplete.

ideas.what: Category whose hom-sets are graded by polynomial degree, with composition multiplying degrees, defined via Γ^n and α_{q,p}: Γ^{pq}→Γ^qΓ^p
ideas.modern_name: category enriched in (N,×)-graded sets / many-object plethory; divided-power category ΓP of strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); Friedlander–Suslin (ΓP, strict polynomial functors, 1997); Borger–Wieland (plethories, 2005)

ideas.what: Multihomogeneous decomposition of polynomial maps on a product via the exponential property of Γ
ideas.modern_name: exponential property Γ(V⊕W)=Γ(V)⊗Γ(W); multihomogeneous polynomial laws

ideas.what: Equivalence between abstract 'strict polynomial categories' and additive tensor categories equipped with divided-power functors ('⊗-pd-categories')
ideas.modern_name: representability/reconstruction of polynomial-map enrichment by Γ^n; cf. tensor categories with divided powers
ideas.usually_credited_to: no clear single source; related to Krause, Touzé, Kuhn on ΓP

ideas.what: k-linearity as k→End(id) with multihomogeneity f∘(λ_i)=∏λ_i^{ν_i} f
ideas.modern_name: homogeneity of polynomial laws / weight grading

missed.claim: An abstract axiomatization of 'polynomial categories' (P_n hom-sets, degree-multiplicative composition) and the claim that the strict ones are equivalent to additive ⊗-categories with Γ^n functors. This was intended as a framework for multiplicative structures on perfect complexes and was never written up.
missed.quote: Une catégorie polynomiale P est dite stricte si elle satisfait aux conditions préliminaires permettant de définir ⊗ et Γ^n ... est dite une ⊗-pd-catégorie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the many-object plethory / ΓP viewpoint and the 'polynomial enrichment vs. divided-power functor' duality now used for strict polynomial functors and derived divided powers. A precise statement of this equivalence would be a clean foundational result.

deep.surprise_reason: An early, abstract many-object formulation of polynomial (divided-power) enrichment, predating Friedlander–Suslin's ΓP and Borger–Wieland plethories. However, it is a sketch with incomplete axioms, and the individual ingredients (Roby's laws, the exponential property of Γ) are classical.
transcription_corrections: 'X = ∐ X_i' is written with a boxed ⊕/⊞ symbol (biproduct) indexed 1≤i≤r.
'les produits tensoriels de P,' is likely 'les produits tensoriels de P_1'.
'condition d'associativité préli-' may read 'condition universelle préli-[minaire]'.
'Les deux notions ne diffèrent que par l'équivalence' is uncertain; it may read 'ne diffèrent qu'en apparence' or similar, asserting equivalence.
Last line: 'k → End(id_{P_1}) (où id_{P_1} ...)' – the subscript is P_1, not P.
